jobs.title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
jobs.description:
Creditstar Group is a rapidly growing international consumer finance company, headquartered in Tallinn, Estonia and operating in multiple European markets.

At the core, we are a financial technology company that uses automated processes, algorithms and data analysis to make financial instruments easily available to a population of more than 175 million people in our target markets. We are a team of ambitious professionals who value innovation, effective efficiency, high growth, and high performance. For more information on the group, please visit www.creditstar.com.

Our vision is to build and deliver digital banking products of the future. If you want to be part of this, here is your chance.

YOUR POSITION: FULL STACK ENGINEER

YOUR ROLE:

We are looking for a solution-focused person, who is a great communicator and a team player. Your role is to participate in product and platform development - work closely with the revolving credit product team to develop new features, frameworks and detailed application designs on core architecture of the company’s backend system and develop and maintain scalable software solutions and high-quality web platforms that are built up automation in mind.

YOUR DAILY ACTIVITIES INCLUDE:

  • Designing and coding our backend and frontend systems.
  • Solving technical challenges and fixing bugs.
  • Follow and maintain coding standards and best practices.
  • Conduct functionality testing and write automated tests..
  • Define and document technical solutions and best practices

REQUIREMENTS:

  • Extensive experience with modern PHP, with the ability to leverage the strengths of the language.
  • Good analytical, problem-solving and communication skills.
  • You have a strong passion for technology and love to code.
  • You have worked with relational databases like MySQL or PostgreSQL before.
  • You thrive in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment. You are self-motivated and proactive, able to work independently in a fully remote team setup.
  • Proven ownership mindset—taking initiative, solving problems proactively, and driving solutions forward.

NICE TO HAVE:

  • Experience with the Yii2 framework is a plus.
  • Experience with NodeJS is a plus.
  • Experience with React or other major JavaScript frameworks.
  • Financial service development background.
  • Experience with distributed systems.
  • You love optimization and the beauty of automation.

TOOL STACK:

  • PHP, Yii2, HTML/CSS, Javascript, Typescript, PostgreSQL
  • React, Nodejs, Jquery
  • Docker
  • Atlassian products
  • Datadog, Sentry
  • AWS

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Usercentrics is a global leader in data privacy and privacy-led marketing solutions. We believe there is no need for a trade-off between growth and privacy compliance. Our vision is to unlock the potential of data privacy to empower a thriving digital ecosystem. We work with companies to create a healthy balance between data-driven business and privacy-led marketing for every size of enterprise.

We're hiring a hands-on engineer to build and own production systems across our full stack. You'll ship real features and platform components, hold your work and your team's work to a high quality bar, and grow your technical scope over time.

How we build has changed. You'll spend less time typing syntax and more time specifying intent, directing AI coding agents, and reviewing what they produce.

You own the correctness of everything you ship, whoever or whatever wrote the first draft.

We hire at two levels, Software Engineer and Senior Software Engineer. The level is set during the process based on your experience and the scope you've owned.

YOUR TASKS:

Build, with AI as a core tool

  • Implement features and platform components end-to-end, from design through production.
  • Specify, generate, review, and validate AI-generated code with the same rigor as your own.
  • Write tests, refactor, and improve the codebase as you go.
  • Prototype approaches in real code before committing to them.

Raise the bar on quality

  • Write maintainable, well-tested, production-grade code.
  • Give thoughtful code reviews, with extra scrutiny on AI-assisted changes.
  • Contribute to observability, reliability, security, and CI/CD practices in your team.
  • Share what works (and what doesn't) with AI-assisted development.

Design and decide

  • Design services, APIs, and components within your team's domain.
  • Make pragmatic trade-offs between delivery speed and long-term health, and explain your reasoning.

Understand the product

  • Connect your work to product outcomes and customer impact.
  • Give technical input on scope and prioritization instead of just taking tickets.
  • Work with product and design to keep our data handling compliant and transparent.

jobs.title: QA Engineer for terminal
jobs.description:
Imagine standing at the top of the Empire State Building, taking in the breathtaking view. From the online booking to the seamless entry, every part of your ticketing experience was designed and supported by Ventrata. An industry-leading SaaS platform that helps attractions, tours, and activities to create memorable experiences.

Backed by a passionate team, headquartered in London and with offices in Brno, Lisbon, and remote teams worldwide, we’re expanding rapidly across multiple markets and verticals. Our mission is to help businesses of all sizes scale and grow while preserving their unique identity and spirit.

Be a part of something extraordinary, where your ideas and contributions truly matter. Let’s shape the future of travel together.

About the Role 

We’re looking for a QA Engineer to join the crew behind our Terminal and Kiosk applications—hardware and software used daily by venues around the globe. For this one, we need you on-site in our Brno office because you'll need regular, hands-on access to the actual physical testing devices we use to make our platform tick.

This gig is a solid mix of manual and automated testing. You’ll validate new features through exploratory and manual testing to hunt down edge cases and make sure the user experience is flawless. At the same time, you'll level up our Maestro automation coverage by turning stable, repetitive user journeys into rock-solid automated tests.

We're actually in the middle of rebuilding our Maestro automation framework and evolving our CI/CD pipelines. This means you get a real opportunity to help shape how mobile testing is done across our products. Automation is a huge part of our long-term strategy, but it won't be the only thing you do all day.

The Team you’ll be collaborating directly with developers, product managers, designers, and our QA squad to ensure every release delivers a reliable experience across Android, iOS, and our kiosk platform.

Don't sweat it—you won't be flying solo or figuring it out in the dark. You're joining a solid team of four experienced QA engineers who have your back. They’ll help you get totally familiar with our products, testing strategy, and automation framework.

Want to be part of something extraordinary where your ideas actually matter? Let’s shape the future of travel together.

What You'll Work On

Unlike traditional web QA roles, you'll work with applications running on real devices used by attractions across the globe.

Our platform includes:

  • Terminal – A Flutter application running on Android and iOS, used for ticket sales and validation.
  • Kiosk – A self-service application built with Kotlin Multiplatform, allowing visitors to purchase and manage tickets independently.

You'll also get hands-on experience with:

  • Mobile phones and tablets
  • Self-service kiosks
  • Ticket scanners, printers, and payment devices
  • End-to-end customer journeys across multiple devices
  • Real-world scenarios combining both software and hardware

Every feature you test directly impacts the daily operations of attractions and the experience of thousands of visitors around the world.

Your Responsibilities

  • Perform exploratory and manual testing of new features, bug fixes, and hardware integrations.
  • Expand and maintain our Maestro automation framework by automating stable and repetitive user journeys.
  • Review and update automated tests based on new features, bug reports, and production issues.
  • Validate releases across Android, iOS, and physical devices.
  • Collaborate closely with developers to investigate issues and improve product quality.
  • Think critically about product behaviour, identify inconsistencies, and suggest improvements.
  • Contribute to improving our testing strategy, automation, and overall quality culture.

At Ventrata, quality goes beyond finding bugs. Since you'll be one of the final people validating features before they reach production, we value curiosity, product thinking, and a willingness to ask questions. If something doesn't feel right, we want you to challenge it. Every improvement you make helps create a smoother experience for both venue staff and the thousands of visitors who use our products every day.

Ready to help shape the future of travel experiences? Apply now and be part of something unforgettable.

About Ventrata

Ventrata is an enterprise ticketing platform designed for high-volume attractions, museums, observatory towers, sightseeing tours, and activity operators. Our all-in-one solution powers online, in-person, and third-party sales, and provides robust functionality for resource management, hardware integrations, and 24/7 live support.

Leading brands across diverse verticals trust Ventrata's solutions, and our focus on building long-term connections is key to mutual success. Since 2016, we have worked with many City Sightseeing operations and have teamed up with notable companies like Big Bus Tours and Historic Tours of America. Our recent partnerships, including those with English Heritage, Paradoxon, the Empire State Building, Thames Clippers, and many others established over the past two years, show strong potential to evolve into enduring, long-term relationships. These examples represent just a few of our many collaborations driving the innovation behind the 21 million tickets we sold in 2023 — a 60% increase from the previous year.

What truly sets us apart is our independence — we've been profitable since 2018, with no reliance on venture capital. This financial stability allows us to innovate and grow on our own terms.

We value collaboration and freedom ensuring that every team member has the space to take ownership, be heard, and drive real impact.

jobs.title: Senior Product Data Engineer- Data Insights (remote, Europe)
jobs.description:
Hey, I'm Tadas. I'm hiring a Senior Product Data Engineer for Data Insights, the team that builds Modash's data products.

Modash helps brands find, understand, and work with creators on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. More than 2,700 companies, including Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN, use us to run and grow their creator partnerships.

Data Insights turns raw social media data into the datapoints customers buy: which brands a creator has worked with, how to contact them, where they're based, and which other creators are like them. Most of the work is taking messy public data across 200M+ profiles and making it accurate enough that a brand will act on it.

In this role you'll own datapoints end to end, from the raw signal to what the customer sees, and you'll be judged on their quality.

Why we're hiring

At Modash, the data is the product customers pay for. Brands use our collaboration, contact, and location data to decide which creators to work with, and our largest customers take it in regular bulk deliveries through our API.

We need a senior engineer who can take one of these datapoints from a rough idea to a production pipeline and keep improving it after launch. Right now that means building our own creator-location data, using LLMs to find and validate creator contact emails, and matching sponsored posts to the right brand and its parent company.

You'll join a team of four data engineers who work closely with four backend engineers. You'll make important technical decisions yourself, with strong teammates to back you up, and customers will see what you build.

For a feel of how we build software, read our Engineering Blog.

What you'll own

1. Build the datapoints customers pay for.

You'll turn raw posts, bios, and profile data into signals: brand collaborations, contact details, creator location, related creators, and links between one creator's accounts on different platforms.

2. Make data quality measurable.

Every datapoint we ship has automated quality checks. You'll decide what good looks like for your datapoint, measure it per platform against real coverage numbers, and catch regressions before customers do.

3. Take projects from idea to production.

You'll shape the problem, scope the work, design the architecture, write the code, ship it, and learn from how it performs. We expect senior engineers to own the outcome, even when the problem arrives half-defined.

4. Use LLMs where they pay off.

We run LLM enrichment at large scale. You'll decide where an LLM beats a rule or a simpler model, and work out what it costs across 200M+ profiles before it ships.

What the day-to-day looks like

Most weeks you're on one project for days at a time, with some of your time going to pipeline issues and code review. A typical week might look like this:

  • Monday. You spot-check your datapoint's output and find a quality problem. You write a short plan for fixing it and get feedback from another data engineer before you start.
  • Tuesday. You build the change in PySpark and test it. It's too slow on the full dataset, so you profile the job and fix it.
  • Wednesday. A pipeline failed overnight. You find the cause, ship a fix, and rerun it. In the afternoon you review a teammate's PR, then get back to your project.
  • Thursday. You compare results before and after the change on each platform. One number moves more than expected, and you dig in until you can explain it.
  • Friday. You merge, watch the first production run, and check the quality reports. You answer a question from a backend engineer about the data, then plan next week.

Every meeting needs a reason, and we protect time for focused work. You'll have a short standup, pair with people when it helps, and get long stretches to plan, build, and ship.

jobs.benefitsSection:
What we offer

  • Fully remote in Europe 🏠 Work from wherever you do your best work.
  • Compensation. Your compensation is made up of salary and stock options. As we're growing fast, the stock option package is especially significant. Annual salary range is €100,000 to €130,000. We hire across Europe, so the exact number depends on your location, employment type, skills, and experience.
  • Flexible hours ⏱ We care about outcomes, not when you log on.
  • Unlimited paid vacation 🌴 Take the time you need to stay rested and do great work.
  • Personal development support 🧠 Courses, books, and conferences are on us.
  • Real ownership 💡 Take meaningful customer problems from ambiguity to impact.
  • Regular offsites ✈️ We’re remote-first, but we make time to connect in person.

And a little more about us...

Founded in 2018 by a high-school dropout and a Canadian (yes, we’re also shocked it’s going so well), Modash is building a suite of tools that help brands scale partnerships with online content creators.

2,700+ companies like Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN already use Modash to manage and scale their influencer marketing work. And we're just getting started. Over the coming decade, brand investment in creators will continue to boom, and Modash will be at the centre of it all.

Modash is here to stay. We have 8-figures in ARR across two products, a $12M series A investment, and we are default alive. We are building a company that will still be here in 20 years; not rushing towards an exit.

We’re almost 100 people distributed across 20+ countries, operating with a fast, async-first culture. If you join Modash, you’ll be surrounded by people who truly want to be the greatest at their craft. People who make you better. Interesting people too, who have done everything from building solar cars, to hanging out with Metallica and Bon Jovi.

Come join us. Be great, do great things, create great memories, all while making a great impact. Do it.
jobs.requirementsSection:
What you've done before

  • Built data systems at meaningful scale. You have solid experience as a data engineer and have worked with large, complex datasets in production.
  • Worked deeply with Spark. PySpark, Scala, or Databricks all count. We use PySpark, but strong Spark fundamentals matter more than the exact flavour. Here is the blog post that helps explain the kind of work we do.
  • Turned messy data into signals people rely on. Entity matching, classification, deduplication, or enrichment: you've built reliable output from data that started out incomplete, inconsistent, or wrong.
  • Treated data quality as part of the job. You've defined quality checks, tracked coverage and accuracy, and handled a quality drop like a bug.
  • Owned full features. You've taken a feature through planning, scoping, architecture, implementation, release, and iteration.
  • Written production Python and SQL. You care about code quality, system design, and maintainability.
  • Worked with orchestration and cloud infrastructure. Experience with Airflow or AWS Step Functions, and with services such as EMR, Glue, Athena, DynamoDB, S3, Kinesis, Lambda, or ECS, will help you get moving quickly.
  • Worked using agentic development. You use coding agents like Cursor in your daily work, give them clear context, and review what they write as carefully as a teammate's PR.
  • Worked autonomously without working alone. You make progress with incomplete information, say what you think, ask for feedback, and help teammates do better work.

Curiosity about the creator economy helps too, but we'll get you up to speed.

Our stack

  • AWS, with Pulumi for infrastructure as code
  • Spark on EMR, mostly PySpark
  • Iceberg tables on S3, queried through Glue and Athena
  • PostgreSQL on Aurora
  • Airflow
  • Great Expectations for data quality checks
  • LLM models for data enrichment
  • DynamoDB, Kinesis, Lambda, and ECS
  • GitHub, Notion, Linear, Cursor

The interview process

We move quickly and can finish the process in under a week:

  1. Intro chat
  2. Two technical interviews: an agentic PySpark coding challenge and a system design session
  3. Team fit and project presentation
  4. Culture and alignment conversation with our CEO, Avery Shrader

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Forward Deployed Engineers take a defined use case from nothing to a working, production-grade system inside the customer's environment. That starts with knowing our platform deeply enough to combine its capabilities into solutions more complex than any single feature was designed for - and where a customer's specific needs call for something beyond the standard functionality, building that missing piece themselves. This is the role that builds the use case: not a prototype handed to someone else to production, but the system that goes live. 

This is a customer-facing role. Understanding the customer's needs and the realistic possibilities of their technical environment - and working in close, daily collaboration with them - is what makes a deployment succeed. We're in daily working contact with the customer's engineers and executives, mostly online, with our team and theirs operating as one delivery unit with shared planning. Success is measured on the customer's numbers - resolution rate, containment, response latency, CSAT, cost per contact - and accountability continues past go-live. 

Forward Deployed Engineering brings together two disciplines that used to sit apart: conversation design and integration engineering. An engineer who can build the technical logic behind a scenario; a conversation designer who can design the flow of the conversation itself - that is what an FDE is. We hire people who are genuinely strong in one of the two and want to grow the other - expert in both is a direction of travel, not an entry bar. The role is based in Prague and is part of a global function with teams in EMEA and North America. 

Please note this is a hybrid role with significant customer on-site availability required.

Responsibilities

  • Own the solution design: translate a stated business problem into a technical architecture that fits the customer’s actual processes, constraints and systems. 
  • Build the agent 0→1: design, build and iterate the first working version end to end - the system that goes into production, not a hand-off. 
  • Close product gaps: build the custom extensions, integrations, services and tooling the deployment requires, without waiting for core roadmap prioritization. 
  • Own the integration surface: systems of record, contact channels and data flows - and, for voice deployments, the telephony path from carrier to agent. 
  • Evaluate, iterate, improve: define the workflow-specific tests that determine whether this deployment actually works, and iterate against real traffic until the numbers move. 
  • Work as the customer’s technical counterpart: deploy alongside their engineers, monitor against the agreed KPIs, tune, and stay accountable past go-live. 
  • Feed the platform: capture what you built as a reusable pattern and push recurring patterns toward the core product - the field is our sensing arm.

jobs.title: Technical Support Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Summary

As a Technical Support Engineer at CallMiner, you will help our customers solve complex technical issues across our conversation intelligence, analytics and CX automation products, including OmniAgent. 

This is not a traditional helpdesk role. When a customer tells us, “the bot behaved strangely yesterday”, “this integration stopped working” or “the numbers in last week's report don't look right”, your job is to figure out why. You will investigate real production problems across applications, APIs and integrations, databases, infrastructure, AI and telephony. You may be analyzing logs, tracing API requests, querying data, investigating connectivity, or following SIP communication to understand where a problem occurred. 

You will own issues through resolution and work directly with our Engineering, Infrastructure, Product and Solution Engineering teams when deeper investigation is needed. The position is based in Prague, Czech Republic, and is part of a global team working closely with colleagues in the US and UK. 

Responsibilities 

  • Own and troubleshoot customer-reported technical issues from initial triage through resolution. 
  • Investigate problems across applications, APIs, integrations, databases, infrastructure and telephony using logs, monitoring tools, queries and other available data. 
  • Reproduce issues and distinguish between configuration, integration, infrastructure, customer-side and product problems. 
  • Support the automation side of our portfolio, including conversation flows, agent configuration, API and backend integrations, telephony and connectivity. 
  • Support conversation intelligence and analytics, including data ingestion and capture, transcription, search, scoring, redaction, dashboards and reporting. 
  • Troubleshoot voice and telephony issues using SIP signaling together with application and system logs. 
  • Work directly with Engineering and other technical teams on complex problems and production incidents. 
  • Clearly communicate findings to customers and internal teams and contribute to documentation and improvements to our support processes. 
  • Participate in the team's after-hours and on-call rotation if necessary, responding to paging alerts and critical production issues outside standard business hours as needed.

jobs.title: Software Builder
jobs.description:
Why this job is exciting

We're changing how we build. We're moving from teams where each developer owns a slice of an epic to builders who own the whole thing. A builder takes an idea and ships it: designed, implemented, evaluated, deployed. One person, full ownership, from first commit to production.

Agents made this possible. At Innovatrics, engineers develop with AI agents as the default way of working: you direct the work, the agents produce much of the code, and you own the result. Claude Code is our standard. The craft is judgment: knowing what to delegate, what to verify, what to build by hand, and how to prove the result is correct.

That last part is the heart of this job. We build biometric identity systems used by governments, banks, and security agencies: face recognition, fingerprint matching, identity verification at airports, at borders, in banking apps. This domain is regulated and adversarial. People probe our systems to defeat them. So we ship what we can stand behind, and proving correctness is part of the craft here, with the same weight as writing the code.

Where this sits

These roles map to the Software Engineer and Senior Software Engineer bands of our career framework. We'll calibrate level together during the process, based on the scope of ownership you've actually carried. The framework runs to Distinguished Principal, and the growth path is real.

What you'll be doing

  • Owning features end to end: design, implementation, evaluation, deployment. Done means running in production.
  • Directing AI agents through most of the build, then verifying the output as if you wrote every line yourself. You own agent output the same way you own your own code.
  • Writing evals as part of delivery, so correctness is demonstrated rather than assumed.
  • Improving the shared machinery: when an agent makes the same mistake twice, the context, prompt patterns, or harness gets fixed so it can't recur, for the whole team.
  • Making deliberate calls on when AI is the wrong tool: security-sensitive code, novel biometric algorithms, deep-system work.
  • Working across the stack your product needs, going wherever the problem is rather than waiting at a layer boundary.
  • Collaborating with product and other engineers when you need input, without waiting for permission to move.

What we offer

  • Direct impact: your work ships to global customers and gets used in the field.
  • A culture that trusts you to own your work.
  • Hybrid work from our Bratislava office, with flexibility on days and hours.
  • Competitive salary benchmarked to market, reviewed annually.
  • Hardware of your choice and a full AI tooling budget. We pay for the tokens; you bring the judgment.
  • A team that takes its craft seriously and is honest about what isn't working.

Compensation

At Innovatrics, we offer highly competitive salaries because we value top talent who share our values and goals. Compensation is determined based on your level, skills, experience, qualifications, and location.

💶 Base Salary gross from 3,700 EUR - 5,000 EUR / Month. Compensation is tied to competency and technical evaluation, complemented by an attractive variable compensation scheme and a comprehensive benefits package supporting both your professional growth and well-being.

📈 Beyond base pay, we provide an attractive benefits package. You can learn more at: https://careers.innovatrics.com/benefits/

Interview Process

👋 Introduction Stage (~30 min.)

  • Recruiter Screen

💻 Offline Assignment

  • AI Assignment (3 hours) - A take-home exercise you'll complete independently, designed to assess your problem-solving approach and hands-on technical skills relevant to the role.

🧑‍💻 Onsite Interview (~2 hours)

  • An in-person session with our technical team and Hiring Manager, focusing on your problem-solving approach, technical knowledge, and a walkthrough/discussion of your completed assignment.

🎯 Final Stage (~30 min.)

  • CARES Interview: Final conversation with our CARES committee to ensure alignment with our core values—Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Shared Mission.
  • Reference checks and background verification

We encourage candidates to request additional conversations with anyone they would like to meet.
jobs.requirementsSection:
We hire builders at 2 levels. The core is the same at both; the scope of ownership differs.

  • Solid grounding in system design: you can reason about how a system behaves when things go wrong, including failures, retries, ordering, and scale, and you can defend the trade-offs you choose rather than just listing options.
  • A developer who has shipped real things to real users, and can walk us through what broke and what they learned.
  • Comfort across more than one language or stack, with genuine depth in at least one. Builders range wide; the best ones also go deep where their product demands it.
  • Hands-on experience developing with AI agents (Claude Code or comparable), and a clear-eyed view of what they get wrong: plausible-but-broken logic, invented packages, missed edge cases.
  • The habit of verification: you can say how you know a piece of work is correct, whether you wrote it or an agent did.
  • A bias toward done over perfect, with correctness intact.
  • Comfort with ambiguity: you can take a rough brief, scope it, and figure out the rest.

As a mid-level builder, on top of that:

  • You own complex work autonomously: you take an Epic-sized requirement, structure it, and deliver it with light guidance.
  • You write evals for your own work and invest in the team's shared agent setup beyond your own productivity.
  • You can design a service end to end and stand behind its architecture under pushback, including how it handles failure and what you’d monitor to know it’s stuck.

As a senior-level builder, on top of that:

  • You take a high-impact requirement and turn it into a shipped solution across team boundaries.
  • You help define the team's agent strategy: which problems get agents, which get humans, which get pairs.
  • You own the team's eval discipline and build the harnesses, context files, and agent skills the team depends on.
  • You articulate taste: you can explain why one design beats another, spot hallucinated code in review, and say no with reasons.
  • You develop the engineers around you, deliberately, so they form real skills while agents do the obvious work.
  • You articulate taste: you can explain why one design or architecture beats another, including for distributed systems at scale, spot hallucinated code in review, and say no with reasons.

Good to have

  • Experience with Java, Python, Go, C++, TypeScript, Kotlin, or Swift (different teams use different sets).
  • Familiarity with biometrics, computer vision, or identity verification.
  • Experience building evaluation pipelines, test harnesses, or CI quality gates.
  • Cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP) or container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker).
